# Story 46 — Configure roles and permissions

---

## Prerequisites

- Story 3 (RBAC) completed: `requireAuth` / `requireRole` exist in `backend/src/middleware/auth.ts` and the three-role model (`customer` | `agent` | `admin`) is in `backend/src/models/User.ts`. This story extends both.
- Story 45 (manage user accounts) — sub-admin (and agent) accounts must be creatable there before this story's permission fields have anywhere to live. Story 45 never lets anyone create an `admin` account through the app at all (they're DB-provisioned only, `backend/scripts/seed-admin.ts`) — so there is **no creation-side cap to coordinate** for the `staff:*` keys. The cap this story must respect lives on **status changes**: Story 45's `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/deactivate` must keep `requireRole("admin")` permanently for any target whose `role === "admin"`, even after this story's `requirePermission` exists for the agent/subadmin branch (`staff:toggle_status`). See Task 5 below — this story is the one that actually wires that split in, since Story 45 only left a marked comment for it.
- Coordinate with owners of any route that currently uses `requireRole("admin")` before flipping it to `requirePermission(...)`.

---

## Story Goal

Introduce a fourth role `subadmin` and a live, **granular** permission layer that governs both `agent` and `subadmin` accounts. The full admin (`admin`) is fixed and always passes every permission check — there is nothing to configure for it. Unlike a single shared per-role permission set, permissions in the shipped design are granted **per account**: each `agent`/`subadmin` user document carries its own list of granted permission keys, assigned and edited as a step inside that account's own creation/edit flow (not through a standalone role-level settings screen). A `requirePermission(key)` middleware does a **live DB lookup on every request** against the *calling user's own* stored permissions (no session/JWT caching), so a change an admin makes takes effect on that user's very next request.

The single coarse `users:manage` key from the original design is replaced by six independently-grantable keys in a `staff:*` namespace, each covering one staff-account action instead of all of them at once:

- `staff:view_list` — see the accounts roster table.
- `staff:view_account` — open one account's detail/edit page, read-only.
- `staff:edit` — change an account's name/email/role (this key also gates account **creation** — creating an account is treated as editing a not-yet-existing one).
- `staff:toggle_status` — activate/deactivate an account.
- `staff:delete` — soft-delete an account.
- `staff:permissions` — change an account's granted permissions (the renamed, repurposed successor to the old design's orphaned, unused `users:permissions` key).

**New rule — a hard, server-enforced tier split:** staff/system-administration permissions are **sub-admin only** and can never be granted to an `agent` account. That subadmin-only set is all six `staff:*` keys above, plus `config:edit`, `audit:view`, `sla:configure`, `kb:publish`, and `reports:export` (11 keys total). Everything else in the vocabulary — `customers:manage`, `tickets:delete`, `tickets:reassign`, `tickets:view_all`, `reports:view`, `ai:override_category` (6 keys) — remains assignable to either an `agent` or a `subadmin`. This is enforced **server-side**, not just hidden in the UI: `backend/src/routes/admin.routes.ts`'s `validatePermissions` helper rejects (400) any attempt to assign a subadmin-only key to an account whose role is/becomes `"agent"`, using `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts`'s `SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` set and `permissionKeysAllowedForRole(role)` helper. The account-creation/edit stepper's permissions step (`frontend/app/admin/users/PermissionsStep.tsx`) mirrors this client-side by filtering which permission rows are even shown based on the role picked for the account — an agent's form never displays the subadmin-only rows at all — but the 400 is the real boundary, not the hidden rows.

**Not in scope:** a standalone `/admin/users/permissions` role-configuration screen (superseded by the per-account stepper described above); changing customer-vs-staff route boundaries that are not about admin-vs-sub-admin nuance; account CRUD itself (Story 45) — this story wires the granular permission checks into the endpoints Story 45 already built and adds the fields/step needed to grant permissions per account.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** three roles (`customer` / `agent` / `admin`); admin actions are gated by hardcoded `requireRole("admin")` (or the admin branch of `requireRole("agent","admin")`); there is no way to grant a subset of admin power to anyone.
- **New behaviour:** four roles (`customer` / `agent` / `admin` / `subadmin`); `admin` always passes every permission check; `agent` and `subadmin` accounts each carry their own granted-permission list (`permissions: PermissionKey[]` on the `User` document), assigned/edited per account rather than shared per role; permission changes are picked up on the very next request (no cache).
- **Fixed permission vocabulary, 17 keys** (seed exactly these keys, in this order, as the fixed list the UI offers, grouped by category):
  `staff:view_list`, `staff:view_account`, `staff:edit`, `staff:toggle_status`, `staff:delete`, `staff:permissions`, `audit:view`, `config:edit`, `customers:manage`, `tickets:delete`, `tickets:reassign`, `tickets:view_all`, `sla:configure`, `kb:publish`, `reports:view`, `reports:export`, `ai:override_category`.
- **Subadmin-only tier (11 keys), never assignable to `agent`:** all six `staff:*` keys, plus `config:edit`, `audit:view`, `sla:configure`, `kb:publish`, `reports:export`. Assigning any of these to an `agent`-role account (at creation or edit) is a 400, enforced server-side.
- **Assignable to either `agent` or `subadmin` (6 keys):** `customers:manage`, `tickets:delete`, `tickets:reassign`, `tickets:view_all`, `reports:view`, `ai:override_category`.
- **Defaults are a UI starting point, not a persisted role record:** the account-creation stepper pre-selects `["tickets:reassign", "reports:view", "ai:override_category"]` when the role picked is `agent`, and nothing when the role picked is `subadmin` — the admin can still change the selection before submitting. There is no background "role defaults" document to keep in sync; each account's `permissions` array is simply whatever was submitted (or later edited) for that one account.
- **The cap is on status changes, not creation.** There is no `admin`-creation endpoint anywhere (Story 45 never builds one), so `staff:edit` needs no special carve-out for account creation. The cap instead applies to `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/deactivate` (Story 45): toggling the status of a target whose `role === "admin"` always stays `requireRole("admin")`, independent of `staff:toggle_status`. Do not add a bypass, and do not describe this as a creation-side restriction anywhere in code comments or UI copy — it is specifically about changing the status of an *existing* admin account.

### 2 — Add the permission vocabulary and a `permissions` field on `User`

**Create file:** `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts`

```ts
// Fixed permission vocabulary. Permissions are granted PER INDIVIDUAL
// agent/sub-admin account (stored on User.permissions) — there is no shared
// per-role permission set. The "staff:*" keys replace what used to be a
// single coarse "users:manage" key — every staff-account action (view the
// roster, view one account, edit its details, activate/deactivate, delete,
// change its granted permissions) is now independently grantable.
export const PERMISSION_KEYS = [
  "staff:view_list",
  "staff:view_account",
  "staff:edit",
  "staff:toggle_status",
  "staff:delete",
  "staff:permissions",
  "audit:view",
  "config:edit",
  "customers:manage",
  "tickets:delete",
  "tickets:reassign",
  "tickets:view_all",
  "sla:configure",
  "kb:publish",
  "reports:view",
  "reports:export",
  "ai:override_category",
] as const;

export type PermissionKey = (typeof PERMISSION_KEYS)[number];

export type CreatableStaffRole = "agent" | "subadmin";

// Keys that can only ever be granted to a sub-admin account, never an agent
// — staff/system administration is a sub-admin-tier concern, agents are
// scoped to customer/ticket-facing work. Enforced server-side in
// admin.routes.ts's validatePermissions (not just hidden in the UI).
export const SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS: ReadonlySet<PermissionKey> = new Set([
  "staff:view_list",
  "staff:view_account",
  "staff:edit",
  "staff:toggle_status",
  "staff:delete",
  "staff:permissions",
  "audit:view",
  "config:edit",
  "sla:configure",
  "kb:publish",
  "reports:export",
]);

export function permissionKeysAllowedForRole(role: CreatableStaffRole): readonly PermissionKey[] {
  if (role === "subadmin") return PERMISSION_KEYS;
  return PERMISSION_KEYS.filter((key) => !SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS.has(key));
}

// Suggested starting point when creating a new account via the admin UI's
// stepper (step 2 pre-fill) — a convenience default, not an enforced
// role-level set. The admin can freely adjust before or after creation;
// once created, permissions live entirely on that individual User document.
export const DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS_BY_ROLE: Record<CreatableStaffRole, PermissionKey[]> = {
  agent: ["tickets:reassign", "reports:view", "ai:override_category"],
  subadmin: [],
};
```

**File:** `backend/src/models/User.ts`

- Add `permissions: [{ type: String, enum: PERMISSION_KEYS }]` to the schema (no explicit default needed — an empty array is Mongoose's own default for an array path), and `permissions: PermissionKey[]` to `IUser`. Meaningful only for `agent`/`subadmin` documents — `customer` and `admin` documents simply carry an empty array and it is never read for them (`admin` always short-circuits every check; `customer` never reaches a permission-gated staff route).
- Add `isDeleted: { type: Boolean, default: false }` to the schema and `IUser` — backs the soft-delete action (Task 5) that extends Story 45's account-management surface. A deleted account is excluded from the roster and single-account lookups (`isDeleted: { $ne: true }` in every `admin.routes.ts` query) and fully locked out (`isActive` is also forced `false` on delete), but the document itself is kept for referential integrity (past ticket assignments, audit log entries) — there is no restore action.

There is **no** separate `RolePermissions` collection in this design — permissions are a field on the account itself, not a shared per-role document, so there's nothing to keep in sync across accounts of the same role.

### 3 — Add a `hasPermission` service helper and the `requirePermission` middleware

**Create file:** `backend/src/services/permissions.ts`

```ts
import { User } from "../models/User";
import { PermissionKey } from "../constants/permissions";

// Shared by requirePermission (middleware/auth.ts) and any route that needs
// to check a permission mid-handler rather than as route-level middleware
// (e.g. admin.routes.ts's PATCH /:id/deactivate, which only knows whether
// the check applies once it has loaded the target document). Live DB lookup
// against the CALLER's own User document, no caching — a permission change
// must take effect on the very next request. Permissions are per individual
// account (security-admin Story 46) — there is no role-level fallback.
export async function hasPermission(userId: string, key: PermissionKey): Promise<boolean> {
  const doc = await User.findById(userId).select("permissions").lean();
  return Boolean(doc?.permissions?.includes(key));
}
```

**File:** `backend/src/middleware/auth.ts`

- Import `PermissionKey` from `../constants/permissions` and `hasPermission` from `../services/permissions`.
- Add:

```ts
export function requirePermission(key: PermissionKey) {
  return async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    if (!req.user) {
      res.status(401).json({ error: "Missing or invalid Authorization header" });
      return;
    }
    if (req.user.role === "admin") {
      next();
      return; // admin always passes
    }
    if (req.user.role !== "agent" && req.user.role !== "subadmin") {
      res.status(403).json({ error: "You do not have permission to perform this action" });
      return;
    }
    const granted = await hasPermission(req.user.id, key);
    if (!granted) {
      res.status(403).json({ error: "You do not have permission to perform this action" });
      return;
    }
    next();
  };
}
```

- **Do not** memoise or in-process cache the lookup.
- The JWT access token payload gains two fields purely for UI-only decisions (which nav links/actions to render) — `email` and `permissions` — alongside the existing `sub`/`role`/`name`/`membershipNumber`. **Never use the token's `permissions` claim for authorization** — `requirePermission` above always re-reads the database; the claim exists only so `frontend/lib/jwt.ts`'s `peekJwtPayload()` can decide what to show without an extra round trip, exactly like the existing unverified `role`/`name` peek.
- Update `backend/src/middleware/README.md` with a short `requirePermission(key)` section mirroring the `requireRole` block.

Leave customer-vs-staff `requireRole("customer")` and pure-agent gates alone elsewhere in the app.

**File:** `backend/src/routes/customer.routes.ts`

- Line 40 `router.get("/", requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin"), ...)` → **`agent` and `admin` must keep exactly today's unconditional access — this is a bug fix on the naive conversion, not optional.** `agent`'s stepper-default permission selection (Product rules, above) is `["tickets:reassign", "reports:view", "ai:override_category"]` — it does **not** include `customers:manage`, and an admin creating an agent is free to deselect even those. Gating this route on `requirePermission("customers:manage")` for `agent` too would silently 403 every existing agent the moment this story ships, breaking Story 55's already-working customer roster/creation for anyone who hasn't been individually granted the permission. Compose as:
  ```ts
  requireAuth,
  requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin"),
  (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) =>
    req.user!.role === "subadmin"
      ? requirePermission("customers:manage")(req, res, next)
      : next(), // agent and admin keep unconditional access, unchanged from today
  ```

### 5 — Convert Story 45's `admin.routes.ts` TODO markers, and add the actions/fields Story 45's own plan didn't spell out

**File:** `backend/src/routes/admin.routes.ts` (Story 45's file — implement Story 45 first if it hasn't landed, or read its plan per Context item 6 to know the exact shape to edit; note Story 45's *shipped* scope is already wider than its own plan document — see that plan's "Scope note" — including `GET /:id`, `PATCH /:id`, `PATCH /:id/activate`, and `DELETE /:id`. This story's job is to gate all of it with the granular permission model, not to build those endpoints from scratch.)

Two small helpers used throughout the router:

```ts
// `targetRole` is the role the account HAS (edit) or WILL HAVE (create, when
// changing role) — a subadmin-only permission is never valid on an agent,
// checked here as well as filtered out client-side, since the UI
// restriction alone isn't a real boundary. Returns the deduplicated,
// validated array, or null if the input is malformed / not allowed.
function validatePermissions(input: unknown, targetRole: UserRole): PermissionKey[] | null {
  if (input === undefined) return [];
  if (!Array.isArray(input) || !input.every((k) => typeof k === "string")) return null;
  if (!input.every((k) => (PERMISSION_KEYS as readonly string[]).includes(k))) return null;
  if (targetRole === "agent" && input.some((k) => SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS.has(k as PermissionKey))) return null;
  return Array.from(new Set(input)) as PermissionKey[];
}

// Shared by every action below whose real permission decision depends on the
// TARGET's role, not just the caller's — the target isn't known until the
// document loads, so this can't be plain route-level middleware. Returns
// true if the caller is allowed to perform `requiredKey` on `target`.
async function canManageTarget(
  callerId: string,
  callerRole: UserRole,
  target: IUser,
  requiredKey: PermissionKey
): Promise<boolean> {
  if (callerRole === "admin") return true;
  if (target.role === "admin") return false; // hard cap — never delegable, see Story 46
  return hasPermission(callerId, requiredKey);
}
```

Conversions/additions, by endpoint:

- **`GET /`** (roster) — `requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin"), requirePermission("staff:view_list")`. `admin` still passes via the middleware's own short-circuit. Query filter adds `isDeleted: { $ne: true }` so a soft-deleted account never appears.
- **`GET /:id`** (single-account detail) — `requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin"), requirePermission("staff:view_account")`. Returns the same shape as a roster row plus the account's `permissions` array (never `passwordHash`). Backs `frontend/app/admin/users/[id]/edit`'s read-only view. 404s (not the malformed-id 400) for a soft-deleted target, same as a nonexistent id.
- **`POST /`** (create agent/subadmin) — `requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin"), requirePermission("staff:edit")`. No admin-target cap needed here — `CREATABLE_STAFF_ROLES` already excludes `"admin"`, so there's nothing for a delegated sub-admin to escalate into via role — but the request body's optional `permissions` array is still run through `validatePermissions(permissions, role)`, 400 on an unknown key or a subadmin-only key submitted against `role: "agent"`.
- **`PATCH /:id`** (edit name/email/role **and** permissions — one combined endpoint, not two) — `requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin")`; the real decision happens inside the handler because it depends on *which* fields are present and on the *target's* role:
  - 400 (not 403/404) if the target's current `role === "admin"` — admin accounts aren't editable through this endpoint at all, full stop, regardless of the caller's own role or permissions.
  - Otherwise: if the body touches `name`/`email`/`role`, require `canManageTarget(caller, target, "staff:edit")`; if it touches `permissions`, require `canManageTarget(caller, target, "staff:permissions")` — independently, so a caller can hold one without the other and the request 403s only if it touches a section they can't act on.
  - `permissions` (if present) is re-validated with `validatePermissions(permissions, resultingRole)`, where `resultingRole` accounts for a `role` change in the same request — so moving an account from `subadmin` to `agent` while its `permissions` array still holds a subadmin-only key is rejected with 400 rather than silently saved.
- **`PATCH /:id/deactivate`** and **`PATCH /:id/activate`** — two endpoints sharing one `setActiveState(req, res, isActive)` helper. Both: `requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin")` at the route level only (same reasoning as `PATCH /:id` — the target's role isn't known until the document loads); inside the helper, `canManageTarget(caller, target, "staff:toggle_status")` decides 200 vs. 403. This is where Story 45's marked-but-inert admin-target comment becomes load-bearing: `canManageTarget` returns `false` outright whenever `target.role === "admin"` and the caller isn't a true admin, regardless of any granted `staff:toggle_status`.
- **`DELETE /:id`** (soft-delete, new in this story) — `requireAuth, requireRole("agent", "admin", "subadmin")`; inside the handler, `canManageTarget(caller, target, "staff:delete")` — same admin-target hard cap as above. Sets `isDeleted: true`, `isActive: false`, and (for an `agent` target) `isOnline: false`; responds `204`.

`hasPermission` (Task 3's service helper) is what `canManageTarget` calls for the non-admin-target branch — the same function `requirePermission` uses, so the live-lookup logic isn't duplicated or awkwardly composed by invoking Express middleware outside the middleware chain.

### 6 — No standalone permissions-configuration API

Unlike the earlier per-role design, this story does **not** add a `permissions.routes.ts` with `GET /permissions` / `PUT /permissions/:role`. Permissions are read and written as part of the account resource itself (Task 5's `GET /:id` and `POST /`/`PATCH /:id`, the latter accepting a `permissions` field alongside the basic fields) — there is no separate resource to mount in `backend/src/app.ts` for this story.

### 7 — No seed script

Because permissions are per-account rather than per-role, there is no `RolePermissions` collection to seed and no `seed-role-permissions.ts` script. `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS_BY_ROLE` (Task 2) is consumed directly by the frontend stepper (Task 8) as its initial selection — nothing to run against the database.

```ts
export const PERMISSION_CATEGORIES: Record<string, string[]> = {
  staff: ["staff:view_list", "staff:view_account", "staff:edit", "staff:toggle_status", "staff:delete", "staff:permissions"],
  audit: ["audit:view"],
  config: ["config:edit"],
  customers: ["customers:manage"],
  tickets: ["tickets:delete", "tickets:reassign", "tickets:view_all"],
  sla: ["sla:configure"],
  kb: ["kb:publish"],
  reports: ["reports:view", "reports:export"],
  ai: ["ai:override_category"],
};

export const SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS = new Set<string>([
  "staff:view_list", "staff:view_account", "staff:edit", "staff:toggle_status",
  "staff:delete", "staff:permissions", "audit:view", "config:edit",
  "sla:configure", "kb:publish", "reports:export",
]);

export function stripSubadminOnlyPermissions(permissions: string[]): string[] {
  return permissions.filter((key) => !SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS.has(key));
}
```

Mirrors `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts` — kept as a plain hardcoded duplicate (same convention as role labels already duplicated in the frontend's i18n messages) rather than fetched from an API, since the vocabulary is fixed and rarely changes.

**Create file:** `frontend/app/admin/users/PermissionsStep.tsx`

- Client component, shared by both the creation flow (`frontend/app/admin/users/new/NewStaffAccountForm.tsx`, Story 45) and the edit flow (`EditStaffAccountForm.tsx`, below). Props: `value: string[]`, `onChange: (next: string[]) => void`, `disabled?: boolean`, `role: "agent" | "subadmin"`.
- Renders `PERMISSION_CATEGORIES` as a 2-column grid of `<Label>`-wrapped `<Switch>` rows grouped under a category heading; **filters which rows are even shown** by `role` — for `role === "agent"`, `SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` rows are dropped from each category before rendering (a category left with nothing to show is omitted entirely), not just disabled. Labels come from a new `Permissions` i18n namespace (`categories.*`, `keys.*` — Task 11).
- The parent form owns `value`/`onChange` as local state and serializes it into a hidden `<input type="hidden" name="permissions" value={JSON.stringify(permissions)} />` inside the same `<form>` — permissions travel as one more field of the same Server Action submission, not a separate request. When the role `<Select>` changes to `"agent"` mid-edit, the parent strips any already-selected subadmin-only keys via `stripSubadminOnlyPermissions` so the hidden state can't silently retain a now-disallowed key.

**Update `frontend/app/admin/users/new/NewStaffAccountForm.tsx`** (Story 45) — becomes a two-step, numbered stepper (`StepIndicator`): step 1 is the existing name/email/role/password fields, step 2 is `PermissionsStep` (initial `value` computed by the page/form from `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS_BY_ROLE[role]`, or simply started empty client-side and left to the admin — either is acceptable, the acceptance criterion is only that `agent` starts non-empty and `subadmin` starts empty by default). One submit action for both steps; nothing is sent to the backend until step 2's submit.

**Create file:** `frontend/app/admin/users/[id]/edit/page.tsx`** (Server Component) — reachable by an `admin` or a `subadmin` holding `staff:view_account` on their own token (an unverified UI-only peek; the real boundary is the backend). Fetches `GET /api/v1/admin/users/:id`; a 403 (no `staff:view_account` at all) redirects to `/dashboard`, same reasoning as the roster page. If the fetched account's `role === "admin"`, redirects to `/admin/users` instead of rendering the form — admin accounts aren't editable through this UI at all (matches the backend's `PATCH /:id` 400 for the same case). Otherwise computes `canEditDetails = isAdmin || permissions.includes("staff:edit")` and `canEditPermissions = isAdmin || permissions.includes("staff:permissions")` from the peeked JWT and passes them down.

**Create file:** `frontend/app/admin/users/[id]/edit/EditStaffAccountForm.tsx`** (Client Component) — the same two-step stepper shape as the (also updated) creation form, minus the password field, prefilled from the fetched account. Takes `canEditDetails`/`canEditPermissions` as props:
- Step 1's fields (name/email/role) are `disabled={!canEditDetails}`.
- Step 2's `PermissionsStep` is `disabled={pending || !canEditPermissions}`.
- The footer's submit control only renders if `canEditDetails || canEditPermissions` — otherwise a plain "view only" message renders in its place, so a viewer holding neither still reaches the page (via `staff:view_account`) and sees a fully read-only, but still legible, account summary, while a viewer holding exactly one sees that one section interactive and the other disabled.
- The single Server Action submission (Task 9) always sends both `name`/`email`/`role` and `permissions` together — the backend's `PATCH /:id` (Task 5) independently checks `staff:edit` vs. `staff:permissions` per section of the body, so a viewer who can only touch one section simply never changes the other section's disabled fields, and the request still succeeds for the section they're allowed to touch.

**Update `frontend/app/admin/users/page.tsx`** (Story 45's roster) — computes `canEdit`/`canToggleStatus`/`canDelete` from the peeked JWT (`isAdmin || permissions.includes(...)`) and a combined `showActionsColumn = canEdit || canToggleStatus || canDelete`; the Actions column header/cell is omitted entirely (not rendered empty) when `showActionsColumn` is false. Passes all three booleans into a new `RowActions.tsx` component per row.

**Create file:** `frontend/app/admin/users/RowActions.tsx`** (Client Component) — renders, per row: an edit icon-button linking to `/admin/users/[id]/edit` when `canEdit && role !== "admin"` (an `admin` row never gets an edit affordance at all, matching the backend's flat 400 on editing one); an activate-or-deactivate icon-button (via a shared `ConfirmActionButton.tsx` confirmation-dialog wrapper) when `canToggleStatus`, shown for `admin` rows too since the backend enforces the cap there; and a delete icon-button (same `ConfirmActionButton`) when `canDelete`, also shown for `admin` rows for the same reason.

**Access-denied pattern for this feature area:** every staff page a viewer's role/permissions don't cover — `/admin/users`, `/admin/users/[id]/edit`, `/admin/users/new`, and `/customers` — redirects to `/dashboard` instead of rendering a "you don't have access" message.

### 9 — Server actions

**Update `frontend/app/admin/users/new/actions.ts`** (Story 45) — the create Server Action's `zod` schema gains a `permissions` field: `z.string().transform((val, ctx) => { try { const parsed = JSON.parse(val); if (!Array.isArray(parsed) || !parsed.every(p => typeof p === "string")) throw new Error(); return parsed; } catch { ctx.addIssue(...); return z.NEVER; } })`, reading the hidden input's JSON-serialized array (`z` can't validate a `string[]` straight out of `FormData`). Included as-is in the `POST /api/v1/admin/users` body.

**Create file:** `frontend/app/admin/users/[id]/edit/actions.ts`

- `updateStaffAccount(userId, prevState, formData)` → validates `{ name, email, role, permissions }` (same JSON-string transform as above) and calls `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id`, same token-refresh-and-retry-once pattern as every other Server Action in this codebase. Surfaces the backend's 409 (email in use) distinctly; any other non-ok response surfaces `data.error` as a generic message — this is the one place the UI's row-filtering/section-disabling (Task 8) has a real server-side backstop (e.g. a role changed underneath a stale form, or a stale set of subadmin-only keys survives a race), so this error path is reachable and must show a real message, not assume "can't happen."
- On success, `redirect("/admin/users")`.

**Update `frontend/app/admin/users/actions.ts`** (Story 45) — `deactivateStaffAccount`/a new `activateStaffAccount` share one `setStaffAccountActive(userId, isActive)` helper calling `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/activate` or `.../deactivate`; a new `deleteStaffAccount(userId)` calls `DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/:id`. All three: no redirect (stay on the roster), `revalidatePath("/admin/users")` on success, and surface the backend's 403 distinctly (e.g. `t("cannotActOnAdmin")`) for the case a caller's own permission doesn't cover the specific admin-target they clicked on — not always reachable (the row's own icon visibility usually already matches what the viewer can do), but kept honest rather than assumed unreachable.

### 10 — Sidebar / navigation

No new nav entry — there is no standalone `/admin/users/permissions` page in this design. The existing `"accounts"` nav item (`frontend/lib/staffNav.ts`'s `STAFF_NAV_ITEMS`, shared by the desktop rail and the mobile drawer) is already visible to both `admin` and `subadmin` roles unconditionally — it is **not** further gated by `staff:view_list` at the nav level; a `subadmin` who clicks through without that permission simply hits the page's own 403→redirect-to-`/dashboard` behavior (Task 8), the same graceful-degradation the `"customers"` nav item already relies on for a non-staff viewer. No change needed here beyond confirming that existing behavior still holds once the permission layer exists.

### 11 — i18n

**Files:** `frontend/messages/en.json`, `frontend/messages/ar.json`

- Add a `Permissions` namespace (read via `useTranslations("Permissions")` in `PermissionsStep.tsx`) with:
  - `categories.staff`, `categories.audit`, `categories.config`, `categories.customers`, `categories.tickets`, `categories.sla`, `categories.kb`, `categories.reports`, `categories.ai`
  - `keys["staff:view_list"]` … one label per permission key (all 17, both languages).
- Extend `AdminUsersList` (Story 45) with per-icon action labels and confirmation-dialog copy for each of the three row actions: `edit`, `activate`/`activateConfirmTitle`/`activateConfirmBody`/`activateConfirmAction`/`activateCancel`/`activateFailed`, `delete`/`deleteConfirmTitle`/`deleteConfirmBody`/`deleteConfirmAction`/`deleteCancel`/`deleteFailed`, plus a shared `cannotActOnAdmin` for the 403 case, and new table-column keys (`colMembershipNumber`, `colActions`) reflecting the roster's actual columns.
- Extend `NewStaffAccount` (Story 45) with stepper copy: `stepDetails`, `stepPermissions`, `subheadingPermissions`, `back`, `next`.
- Add a new `EditStaffAccount` namespace mirroring `NewStaffAccount`'s shape minus the password keys, plus `viewOnly` ("You don't have permission to make changes here.") for the disabled-submit-control case.
- No `Nav.permissions` key is needed (superseding the earlier per-role-screen design, which would have added one) — the existing `Nav.accounts` key (Story 45) is unchanged.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Fresh DB, no accounts yet.** Nothing to auto-seed — `permissions` defaults to `[]` on the schema itself, so a freshly created `agent`/`subadmin` document is well-formed even if the creation request omitted `permissions` entirely.
- **Admin toggles a permission mid-request-flight.** Middleware performs a fresh DB read per request against the target user's own document (`backend/src/middleware/auth.ts`'s `requirePermission`), so the next request from that user sees the change. No in-process cache to invalidate.
- **`role === "admin"` short-circuit.** Admin never hits the DB lookup, so a missing/corrupt `permissions` array on some other document cannot lock the admin out. Enforced at the top of `requirePermission` in `auth.ts`.
- **Assigning a subadmin-only key to an `agent` account.** Rejected with 400 from `validatePermissions`, both on `POST /` (create) and `PATCH /:id` (edit, when the request body includes `permissions`) — enforced server-side regardless of what the stepper's row-filtering did or didn't show.
- **Changing an account's `role` from `subadmin` to `agent` in the same `PATCH /:id` request that also submits `permissions`.** `validatePermissions` runs against the *resulting* role (the new `role`, if present in the body, not the account's pre-edit role), so a request that would leave a subadmin-only key on an `agent`-bound account is rejected with 400 outright rather than silently saved.
- **Unknown permission key in a request body.** 400 (`{ error: "permissions must be an array of valid permission keys" }`); enforced by validating against `PERMISSION_KEYS` before write.
- **Duplicate keys in a request body.** Deduplicated server-side before write (`Array.from(new Set(input))`).
- **`staff:toggle_status` (or `staff:delete`) self-escalation attempt against an existing `admin` account.** A sub-admin with `staff:toggle_status`/`staff:delete` tries to act on an existing `admin` account via `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/deactivate`, `PATCH /:id/activate`, or `DELETE /:id` (Task 5) — `canManageTarget` returns `false` outright for any non-admin caller against an `admin` target, so this returns 403 regardless of the granted permission. There is no equivalent creation-side concern (see Product rules — Story 45 never lets anyone create an `admin` account at all).
- **Any non-admin caller attempts `PATCH /:id` against an existing `admin` target.** 400 (not 403) — admin accounts aren't editable through this endpoint at all, for anyone, including a true admin; this is a flat rejection of the *action*, not a permission gate.
- **Viewer holds `staff:view_account` but neither `staff:edit` nor `staff:permissions`.** Reaches `/admin/users/[id]/edit`, sees every field disabled and no submit control in either section — not a 403, a legitimately read-only render.
- **Viewer holds none of `staff:edit`/`staff:toggle_status`/`staff:delete` on the roster.** The Actions column is omitted entirely from the table, not rendered with disabled/empty icons.
- **Sub-admin with no permissions at all.** Every `requirePermission` check returns 403; the roster/edit-page/sidebar reflect this by omitting the corresponding UI rather than showing a disabled affordance that always 403s.
- **Widening `UserRole` breaks a discriminated union elsewhere.** After the change in `User.ts` (or confirming Story 45 already made it), run `npm run build` (or `tsc --noEmit`) in `backend/` to catch any exhaustive-switch that assumed three values. Fix by adding a `subadmin` branch or a `default` case.
- **JWT already contains role.** Widened union is backwards-compatible for `customer`/`agent`/`admin` tokens; new `subadmin` tokens only start appearing once Story 45 creates such users. The new `email`/`permissions` claims are additive and UI-only — a token issued before this story lands simply lacks them until the user's next login/refresh, and `peekJwtPayload()` call sites must treat both as optional.
- **Concurrency on `PATCH /:id`.** Two admins editing the same account's details or permissions simultaneously → last-write-wins is acceptable; rely on the document's own `updatedAt` for auditability. Do not add optimistic locking in this story.

## Test Plan

1. **Unit — `backend/tests/middleware/requirePermission.test.ts`** (new, mirror `requireRole.test.ts`):
   - Admin passes without any permission data present.
   - Agent whose document's `permissions` includes the key passes; without it, 403.
   - Sub-admin with an empty `permissions` array, 403 for every key.
   - `customer` role, 403.
   - Unauthenticated (`req.user` missing), 401.
   - Deleted/missing user document for a non-admin role, 403 (not 500).
2. **Unit — `backend/tests/constants/permissions.test.ts`** (new): `permissionKeysAllowedForRole("agent")` excludes every `SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` entry; `permissionKeysAllowedForRole("subadmin")` returns all 17; `validatePermissions` (wherever it's exported from) rejects an unknown key and rejects a subadmin-only key against `"agent"`.
3. **Integration — extend `backend/tests/routes/rbac.integration.test.ts`**: existing `requireRole` tests still pass after the union widening; add a case proving `agent` and `admin` access to `GET /customers` is **unchanged** (200 with no `customers:manage` grant needed — this is the regression this plan must not introduce), and a case where `subadmin` is allowed only when `customers:manage` is granted (403 without it, 200 with it).
4. **Integration — extend `backend/tests/routes/customer.routes.test.ts`**: `agent` gets 200/201 on `GET /customers` / `POST /customers` **with no permission grant at all** (proves no regression against Story 55's existing behavior); `subadmin` gets 403 without `customers:manage` and 200/201 once granted; `admin` passes regardless.
5. **Integration — extend `backend/tests/routes/admin.routes.test.ts`** (Story 45's test file):
   - `subadmin` granted each individual `staff:*` key → 200/201/204 on exactly the matching endpoint(s) (`staff:view_list` → `GET /`; `staff:view_account` → `GET /:id`; `staff:edit` → `POST /` and `PATCH /:id` with `name`/`email`/`role` in the body; `staff:toggle_status` → `PATCH /:id/deactivate` and `PATCH /:id/activate` against an `agent`/`subadmin` target; `staff:delete` → `DELETE /:id`; `staff:permissions` → `PATCH /:id` with `permissions` in the body) and 403 on the others without those specific grants.
   - `subadmin` with `staff:toggle_status` and/or `staff:delete` granted → **403** against an existing `admin` target on `PATCH /:id/deactivate`, `PATCH /:id/activate`, and `DELETE /:id` — the load-bearing cap this story adds.
   - `subadmin` with `staff:edit`/`staff:permissions` granted → **400** (not 403) attempting `PATCH /:id` against an existing `admin` target — the flat "not editable here" rejection, distinct from the 403 cap on the other three actions.
   - `admin` → 200/204 on the same admin-target actions (except `PATCH /:id`, which 400s for every caller including a true admin), unaffected by the cap.
   - `POST /` and `PATCH /:id` (with `permissions` in the body) with a subadmin-only key against an `agent` role/target → 400.
   - `PATCH /:id` changing `role` from `subadmin` to `agent` in the same request that submits `permissions` still containing subadmin-only keys → 400, proving the resulting-role re-validation runs before the write, not against the pre-edit role.
   - `GET /`, `GET /:id` exclude a soft-deleted account; `PATCH /:id`/`.../deactivate`/`.../activate`/`DELETE /:id` against an already-soft-deleted id → 404, same as a nonexistent id.
6. **Frontend smoke** (manual): a `subadmin` without `staff:view_account` visiting `/admin/users/<id>/edit` is redirected to `/dashboard`; one with `staff:view_account` but not `staff:edit`/`staff:permissions` sees a fully disabled form; one with both can edit fields and toggle permissions independently, each section's submit reflecting only its own permission.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Migration:** deploy backend first (widened enum + `permissions` field + `PERMISSION_KEYS`/`SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` constants + converted routes). Existing `agent`/`admin`/`customer` documents are unaffected by the new field (schema default `[]`); no backfill needed since there's no existing per-role state to migrate away from. Then deploy frontend.
- **Half-applied state:** if backend is deployed but no account has ever had permissions explicitly set, every `agent`/`subadmin` simply has `permissions: []` and gets 403 on every gated action until an admin grants something — an acceptable, safe default (fails closed).
- **Rollback:** revert the `admin.routes.ts` conversions (Task 5) and the two `customer.routes.ts` conversions (Task 4) back to their pre-Story-46 `requireRole` gates; the `permissions` field on `User` can be left in place unused; the `UserRole` union widening is safe to keep even when the middleware is gone. If widening must also be rolled back, first ensure no user document has `role: "subadmin"` — a data check before revert.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `cd backend && npm run build` — no TypeScript errors after the union widening and the new `permissions` field.
2. **Backend tests:** `cd backend && npm test` — all new and existing tests green.
3. **Manual API smoke:** with an admin token, `POST /api/v1/admin/users` with `role: "subadmin"` and a `permissions` array including `staff:view_list` and `config:edit` → 201; the same call with `role: "agent"` and `config:edit` in the list → 400. `PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id` on the created sub-admin with `{ permissions: [...existing, "staff:toggle_status"] }` → 200; that sub-admin can now deactivate an agent (`PATCH /:id/deactivate`) but still gets 403 deactivating an admin, with no restart or re-login needed for the grant to take effect.
4. **Frontend runs:** `cd frontend && npm run dev` — visit `/admin/users/new` as admin, fill the basic fields, use the permissions step (rows filtered by the role radio/select), submit, confirm the account and its permissions were created together; visit `/admin/users/<id>/edit` and confirm the view-only vs. editable behavior matches the viewer's own `staff:edit`/`staff:permissions` grants; visit as a viewer with no relevant permission and confirm a redirect to `/dashboard`.
5. **Regression:** existing customer routes still work for admins and (with `customers:manage` granted) subadmins, unchanged for agents; existing `requireRole("customer")` routes unaffected.
